extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in scientometrics, bibliometrics, information science, and computational citation analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and synthesized criteria for studying what citation counts measure, focusing on features to extract from citing documents (contexts, semantics, locations, polarity), methods (surveys, qualitative interviews, machine learning), and data/metadata requirements for large-scale analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation context
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the textual context surrounding an in-text citation (the sentences/phrases in which a reference is embedded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review emphasizes citation context analysis as a primary feature to understand the relationship between citing and cited documents; large datasets of citation contexts enable more comprehensive studies than were previously possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantics and linguistic patterns in citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the semantic content and linguistic/rhetorical patterns used when authors cite prior work (lexical distribution, n-grams, hedging, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies cited use approaches such as lexical distribution analysis, IMRaD-based analysis, hedging cue frequency, n-gram/rhetorical-structure approaches to capture how citation language signals function and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation location within the citing document
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and analyze where within the citing document (e.g., Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; IMRaD sections; specific paragraph positions) citations occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location is highlighted as a key feature that helps interpret citation function and influence; some studies characterize invariant distributions of references across article structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation polarity (sentiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify citations by polarity: negative, neutral, or positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polarity (sentiment) of citations is a distinct analytic dimension and has been the subject of computational and manual studies; combining polarity with function can improve impact interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation function / purpose classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the rhetorical/functional role of a citation (e.g., background, use of method, comparison, support, criticism, perfunctory mention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple taxonomies and automated classification approaches exist; the review stresses function classification as central to understanding why papers are cited and to improve indices and retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citer motivation (surveys or interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use surveys or qualitative interviews of authors (citers) to investigate why they cited particular works and to validate inferred functions/motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes citer motivation surveys/interviews as an important complementary method to text-based analyses; figure and sections explicitly include these qualitative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish scientific vs non-scientific citation reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and account for the fact that citations may be made for scientific reasons (conceptual, methodological, empirical) or non-scientific reasons (social, perfunctory, political).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review reiterates earlier findings that papers may be cited for very different scientific and non-scientific reasons, which affects how citation counts should be interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful vs incidental citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate citations that meaningfully reflect intellectual influence from incidental or peripheral citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work on 'identifying meaningful citations' and 'incidental or influential?' is cited; distinguishing these types is important for assessing true impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence of citations within a single article
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how often a cited work is referenced multiple times within the same citing document (recurrence) as an indicator of influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurrence has been studied as a micro-level feature (e.g., recurrence in physics papers) and can help quantify sustained influence within an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of computational and machine learning techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply machine learning and natural language processing methods to classify citation function, polarity, and influence at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review reports many recent studies using computational approaches (convolutional neural networks, ensemble self-training, NLP-driven analyses) and notes that automated recognition of citation functions has strong potential to enhance citation indices and retrieval—while also attempting to overcome methodological weaknesses of earlier work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and metadata quality / machine-readable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure access to rich metadata and machine-readable full texts to permit large-scale citation context analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical developments (richer metadata and machine-readable formats) in the last decade have enabled citation-context analyses of large datasets; data accessibility and quality are thus foundational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and relational factors (trust, authority, co-authorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider social-network and relational influences on citation behavior, such as trust, authority, and relationships between citing and cited authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review cites studies examining social circles behind references and the role of trust/authority, indicating these are important explanatory variables when interpreting citation counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication outlet effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for how the choice of publication venue (journal/outlet) influences citation behavior and counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies referenced show outlet effects on authors' citation practices and the influence of journal reputation on citation rates; outlet should be treated as a factor in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/article/journal-level factors affecting citation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Include attributes such as author prominence, article type (method vs non-method), journal, and article characteristics when modeling citation counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review and cited literature identify multiple covariates (author, journal, article type) that shape citation accrual and should be included or controlled for in impact analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify citation accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the correctness and fidelity of citations (do cited claims and bibliographic details match the cited source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review cites work on verification of citations (e.g., 'Verification of citations: Fawlty Towers of knowledge?') as a caution and quality-control criterion—mis-citations undermine interpretation of citation-based metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications to information retrieval and impact measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use findings from citation context, function, and polarity analyses to improve information retrieval, article ranking, and measures of academic influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review highlights applied studies that exploit citation contexts for retrieval, ranking, and identifying discoveries, suggesting analytic choices should be evaluated by their utility in downstream IR/impact tasks.
